population.note: FICTIONAL. Adults ≈276M. Current users: 32.5% ≈ 89.7M. Ever-users: 43.0% ≈ 118.7M. Used and off now: 10.5% ≈ 29.0M. Never used: ≈157M. Cycling: ever 43.0 − current 32.5 = 10.5 pts off now. About 16.0 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and about 4.5 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once before stopping again, so (16.0 + 4.5) / 43.0 ≈ 48% have cycled. That is consistent with the parent's ~35% one-year persistence, rising to ~45–50% under gated plans, and with 36–47% restarting within a year. Ever-use rose 7.5 pts (≈20.7M first-time starters), the same as the rise in current use. Most of the net gain in current use came from first-time Medicaid users in the nine newly adopting states, ageing-in to Medicare, and the gray market. Lapsed users re-entering through the AUD route offset stops caused by gating and bone pauses. Age check: 18–29: 18% × 52M = 9.4M. 30–49: 36% × 91M = 32.8M. 50–64: 48% × 62M = 29.8M. 65+: 25% × 71M = 17.75M. Total ≈ 89.7M ≈ 32.5%. 65+ use rose from 17% to 25% as people aged into Part D's permanent obesity benefit. It did not rise further because about one in five 65+ ever-users is on a medically advised pause and DEXA waits slow restarts. 18–29 use rose fastest in relative terms, through gray-market vials and AUD-route telehealth. Income: the bottom third is at 29%, up from 21%, through Medicaid in 40 states plus DC and through gray product. Gray users are under-counted in surveys, so the bottom-third figure is probably low. Off-drug populations: ≈29M ex-users, the largest groups being people cut by gating, people on bone pauses, GI quitters (a group now courted by plaintiffs' firms) and refusers by conviction. Never-users skew under-30, rural, residents of the 10 non-adopting states, and people with contraindications. Pediatric: 1.3% of ~73M ≈ 950k, mostly adolescents 12+ on Medicaid EPSDT and commercial plans. The adolescent bone-accrual question is still open. About two in five children live with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The Part D obesity benefit is unchanged: BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity; $199 negotiated rate; $50 copay; counselling visit; continuation standard; 90-day bone-pause code. Medicare pays 21.5% of fills ≈ 19.25M users (17.75M aged 65+ plus ≈1.5M disabled under-65). That splits into ≈6.6M diabetes, ≈12.2M obesity-benefit users and ≈0.45M AUD-primary users. Since the Nov 2033 CMS guidance, AUD-primary use is covered under standard Part D as a compendia-supported indication, outside the continuation standard. Obesity benefit: 12.2M × $199 × 12 ≈ $29.1B gross, less copays of 12.2M × $50 × 12 ≈ $7.3B, leaves ≈$21.8B/yr to the program, against the CBO's ~$14B/yr average from 2031. All Medicare incretin fills: 19.25M × $199 × 12 ≈ $46.0B gross. Medicaid: nine more states took the 90% enhanced match in 2033 sessions, so 40 states plus DC now participate. Medicaid pays 16.7% of fills ≈ 15.0M users × $199 × 12 ≈ $35.8B gross before supplemental rebates. ≈0.6M of those are AUD-primary users covered under state SUD benefits without weigh-ins. Taken together, public programs pay 38.2% of fills (34.25M users) and are now the default payer for anyone over 65 or low-income.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, generic oral semaglutide, and liraglutide–semaglutide combinations. India also exports finished semaglutide pens to Gulf and African markets. China: generic semaglutide, domestic tirzepatide copies, and research-grade retatrutide and cagrilintide API, which underlies most US gray vials. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 45–75/month, and the main source of US cross-border buying. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics, and Mexico's border pharmacies stock them openly.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Stalled. The 2033 US generic semaglutide entry date set by the Sep 2031 settlements passed with no product. In Apr 2033 FDA issued complete response letters to the first four ANDAs, citing peptide-related impurity and immunogenicity comparisons for synthetic semaglutide against the rDNA reference. Resubmissions need new data, and the earliest plausible launch is 2035. HHS did not reopen price talks. Portal prices therefore stay as they were: injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $199–279, orals $149–199, retatrutide $399 direct and $1,499 list, amycretin $449 direct. PBM net is ≈$170–190. Payer mix of ≈89.7M users: commercial/other (incl. VA/TRICARE) 38.4% = 34.45M; Medicare 21.5% = 19.25M; Medicaid 16.7% = 15.0M; cash/direct 15.6% = 14.0M, including ≈5.0M 'calm', 'focus' and 'Unhooked' subscribers; gray/imported/counterfeit 7.8% = 7.0M. Total 89.7M = 100%. The gray 7.0M breaks down as ≈3.0M on imported Indian or Canadian generic semaglutide, ≈2.4M on 'research-use' retatrutide or cagrilintide vials from US-facing peptide clinics, and ≈1.6M on gray tirzepatide and counterfeit branded pens. About 75% of covering employers still use outcome-gated designs with no bone-pause exemption. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand. The gray regrowth happened outside both, through 'not for human consumption' sales and offshore telehealth.

GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance dose)

GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder in adults, regardless of BMI (semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly injection; ASAM guideline endorsement Jun 2033; FDA approval Sep 2034)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscriptions (low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo, ≈5.0M subscribers including 'Unhooked'), in standard employer lifestyle catalogues
'drink less' use below the AUD diagnostic threshold, often coded as mild AUD
oral semaglutide for AUD (the label covers only the injectable)
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS-endpoint trial reads out 2035)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. next_gen_launch = none: no new class reached market. MariTide got a complete response letter in Mar 2033, with FDA asking for longer BMD data and dose-tolerability data. Amgen resubmitted in Jun 2034, and a decision is expected in 2035. Survodutide received an early-2033 complete response letter citing heart-rate and hepatic-safety questions at top doses. It was resubmitted in 2034 for MASH first, with a decision in 2035. Bimagrumab combinations finished phase 3 without filing, and Lilly guides to a 2035 submission. The new_indications driver was met through an existing product. Two phase 3 trials of semaglutide 2.4 mg in AUD read out in 2032–33, showing about 25–30% fewer heavy-drinking days than placebo with an effect independent of BMI. ASAM endorsed it in Jun 2033, Novo filed an sNDA in Jul 2033, and FDA approved it in Sep 2034, 14 months after filing. The label carries a reward-related adverse-event section drawing on SHAPS data. A tirzepatide AUD phase 3 is ongoing. Retatrutide 12 mg allocation eased from mid-2034 as the Concord NC fill-finish line came up. Incretin market ≈$189B US in 2034 (≈82.7M paying users × ≈$190 average net × 12), and ex-US ≈$25B is still eroding.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Risk is higher during 12 mg retatrutide escalation and with self-dosed gray vials.
Rising in absolute numbers as the 65+ user base grows and high-dose triple-agonist use continues.
A 2034 pooled analysis again finds no clear causal excess, and absolute risk remains low. Mass-tort advertising has sharply increased reporting, and gray-vial cases confound attribution.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. Claims are consolidated in the federal GI MDL, where pancreatitis is the second-largest claim category.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis persisting after discontinuation, ileus and bowel obstruction (mass-tort scale)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. More than 52,000 filed federal cases and about 140,000 tolled claims by end-2034. The first bellwether (Mar 2034) returned a $41M plaintiff verdict and the second (Jun 2034) a defence verdict. Epidemiology supports delayed gastric emptying during use, but persistence after stopping is unresolved.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA added label language on ileus and post-discontinuation symptom reports in 2033 without making a causal determination. Novo and Lilly have disclosed litigation provisions. There is no settlement framework.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Retained gastric contents at anaesthesia. It became more visible as one in three surgical adults is a user, and it is cited in MDL complaints.
With 17.75M users aged 65+, the updated Medicare claims estimate is ≈1.8M long-term older users meeting sarcopenia criteria. In untrained users over 50, lean mass makes up ~30–40% of weight lost.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label. Body-composition monitoring is in the 12 mg retatrutide and amycretin labels. The CMS continuation standard requires annual DEXA for 65+ users on therapy more than 2 years. MA strength benefits continue.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈8.5M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. At a ~0.6%/yr baseline × 0.35 excess, that implies ≈17,800 excess hip fractures a year against ~305,000 US total, plus excess vertebral fractures in cycling postmenopausal women aged 50–64. DEXA waits are 10–18 weeks in the Sun Belt and Midwest, slightly better as mobile capacity grows.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained. Bone endpoints are required in all filings, and they were the reason for the MariTide CRL. The CMS bone-pause code continues, and private gated plans are still not bound by it. The DOJ civil case against Novo is unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict and absolute risk is very low. NAION is now a minor claim category in the MDL.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, including in the AUD trial populations.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: In retatrutide 12 mg users, ~12% cross the SHAPS threshold versus ~5% of comparators. The AUD trials found smaller excesses at 2.4 mg semaglutide, ~7% versus ~4%. In Feb 2034 the first independent survey of low-dose 'calm' subscribers (n≈4,000) found a 6% versus 4% difference that did not reach significance.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The AUD label includes a reward-related adverse-event section, which is the first label mention. The FTC orders against anxiety claims stand. 'Calm', 'focus' and, since Sep 2034, on-label 'treatment for alcohol use disorder' claims are permitted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Millions of regain episodes a year from gating, bone pauses and GI quitting. Some cut-off users re-enter through the AUD route.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The CMS bone-pause code softens regain for Medicare. The Seventh Circuit has not ruled on the Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency in high-loss older users. A new pattern of thiamine concern appears in AUD users who eat little.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance. ASAM AUD guidance adds thiamine and nutrition screening. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of follow-up. The adolescent BMD subset signal persists in the second interim readout and is still small-sample. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Full adolescent data are due to FDA in 2034, and sponsors have asked for a 2035 extension.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Users rose from ≈3.8M to ≈7.0M. Poison-centre incorrect-dosing calls are up about 60% since 2032, with infection and reconstitution errors. Vial-and-syringe use has returned at scale for the first time since 2025.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts and seizures continue, along with the May 2034 DOJ action against the Tampa peptide network. The 'Safe Pens' bill is still stalled. Individuals are not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.effect: Unapproved molecule exposure via 'research-use' vials (gray retatrutide outside label doses, cagrilintide monotherapy, stacked regimens)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. ≈2.4M users. Case series report tachycardia, severe dysesthesia and dehydration at self-titrated doses above 12 mg equivalent, and endotoxin contamination in some lots. None of these users have DEXA or SHAPS monitoring.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warning letters to more than 40 'peptide clinic' operators, and one criminal case. No scheduling.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg and at gray-market doses; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain higher in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use, and the absolute count is rising with the 65+ base.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening is mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: DEXA cohorts confirm the 2032 pattern, which is worst in over-50s cut off by gated plans.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint guidance discussion; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A mean rise of several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide, larger in gray-vial users. Arrhythmia significance unclear.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled precaution; cardiovascular outcomes trial ongoing, readout 2035.

food_and_beverage.state: With one adult in three on the drug, salty snacks are down ~4%/yr and confectionery ~5%/yr. A third large group sold its candy brands to private equity in 2033. Bone-forward dairy, protein lines and thiamine-fortified 'recovery' drinks lead growth. 'On-plan' aisles are standard.

alcohol.state: Seventh straight year of spirits volume decline, now ~4%/yr after AUD use took the heaviest drinkers out of the market. The top decile of drinkers was about half of volume. Beer is down ~3%/yr. Wisconsin and Upper Midwest taverns are closing at roughly twice the pre-2028 rate, and two national distributors merged in 2034. Brewers sell 'one good drink' and non-alcoholic lines and fund 'moderation, not medication' campaigns.

restaurants.state: Spend per cover in high-uptake suburbs is down ~10–12% from 2028, and bar takings are down further. Bar-dependent formats such as sports bars and late-night venues are losing the most. Gram-priced bowls and half portions are the default. Southern 'no-gram' rooms and weekend 'full table' nights persist.

apparel.state: Size churn continues with gating, pauses and GI quitting. Cycling-sized rental and resale are growing, and mid-market plus inventory is cut again.

fitness.state: DEXA-plus-coaching chains and 'prescribed lifting' in Medicare Advantage are expanding. Mobile DEXA fleets have roughly doubled since 2032, and the shortage of staff qualified for older lifters persists.

insurance.state: Employer coverage is at 68%, and ~75% of it is gated. Pharmacy trend is ~+8% on volume, because the absent generic removed the 2033 relief employers had budgeted for. Some employers have added AUD-route exclusions. Medicare Part A and MA absorb rising fracture and fall costs. Excess-casualty carriers are repricing pharma product liability after the MDL.

pharma.state: Volume is up ~30% at flat prices. Lilly leads, with retatrutide allocation easing. Novo gained AUD exclusivity on semaglutide and kept its pricing after the failed generic entry, but carries the larger MDL exposure. Indian and Chinese generic makers wait on ANDA resubmissions and supply the gray trade. Plaintiffs' firms are a measurable advertising buyer.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Fully normalised. Among adults over 40 on insurance, being off needs a reason. The accepted reasons are 'bone pause', 'lost my plan', 'my stomach' (newly respectable since the lawsuits) and 'by conviction'. Visible regain still reads as a gated-plan drop. Not drinking at a work dinner no longer signals recovery. People assume the drug.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use levels have nearly converged, at 29% in the bottom third against 35% in the top, while the quality of care keeps diverging. Top-third users run 12 mg retatrutide or amycretin with coaching, DEXA and antiresorptives. The bottom third splits between Medicaid kiosk weigh-ins and 'research' vials reconstituted at the kitchen counter after a video call. In Tampa, Houston and Phoenix the peptide-clinic storefront sits next to the vape shop.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals are the norm and hosts plan for 'on' guests. The Wisconsin Friday fish fry survives, but the brandy old fashioned beside it is increasingly non-alcoholic or a single drink. Supper clubs that lived off bar tabs are raising plate prices. Church potlucks and Southern no-gram rooms persist as heritage.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps' on/off/pausing field is used by most profiles. First dates have moved from bars to coffee, climbing gyms and walks. 'Unmedicated' remains a niche filter. Advice columns field complaints about partners who started for drinking and 'came back different'.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Assumed to be managed, and now that includes thirst for drink. The backlash coalition of Atlanta body-sovereignty collectives, Tulsa–Dallas congregations, supplement sellers and disability advocates is stable in absolute size. It has gained recovery-movement allies who object to 'pharmaceutical sobriety', and plaintiffs' ads have given its distrust a new vocabulary.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. About 12% of retatrutide 12 mg users cross the SHAPS threshold, versus ~5% of comparators. With ≈8M on top-dose triple or dual regimens, that implies on the order of 550k excess cases if causal. The AUD trials found a ~3-point excess at 2.4 mg semaglutide. The first independent survey of the ≈5.0M low-dose subscribers found a non-significant 2-point difference. The ≈2.4M users self-dosing research-grade retatrutide are entirely unmeasured.
interior_life.framing: Feature in retail, indication in clinic, side effect in the label. 'Quiet', 'Even' and 'Unhooked' sell calm, focus and craving freedom at $149–199/month. Since Sep 2034 'Unhooked' also runs an on-label AUD intake. A ten-question AUDIT screen by video now leads to a prescription, which blurs wellness subscription into addiction treatment. Users still call the bad version 'the grey'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: 'Focus' subscriptions are routine in white-collar lifestyle accounts. Client entertainment in finance and law has shifted from bars to steak-and-sparkling-water dinners, and some firms quietly reimburse AUD-route prescriptions through EAPs. Fleets and warehouses favour continuous use. Sales and hospitality staff still dose down before peaks. Bartenders and servers lose tips as tables order less.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Nashville's 'written unmedicated' scene persists. Lower Broadway honky-tonks that depended on bar rings raise cover charges or cut live sets, so working musicians lose gigs. Critics keep using 'grey era'. Extreme sports, spicy food, sauna-and-cold-plunge clubs and sober raves keep growing as people look for stronger stimulus.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for dose, subscriptions and now AUD prescriptions. Some couples report that one partner's drinking stopped and so did the fights and the fun. Dose-holiday weekends and pharmacy 'restart' packs are routine.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The 2034 midterms featured 'Where's the generic?' ads from both parties. Plaintiffs' firms and tort-reform groups fight over MDL procedure. The continuation-standard fight continues. A new fight has opened over whether the AUD route is a back door around weigh-ins. Recovery advocates split: some celebrate access and others warn against a 'pharma twelve steps'. Alcohol-state delegations from Wisconsin and Kentucky push for an FTC review of AUD telehealth marketing.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA remains data-demanding. It issued CRLs to the semaglutide ANDAs, MariTide and survodutide; approved the AUD indication with a reward-section label; and added post-discontinuation GI language without a causal finding. Import enforcement is selective: warning letters and one DOJ network case, no individual prosecutions, and no importation law. The FTC acts on claims. No new state conditioning or mandate action this step.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Part D obesity benefit at $199 with a $50 copay. A 90% Medicaid match in 40 states plus DC. AUD use is covered under standard Part D and state SUD benefits under the Nov 2033 CMS guidance. No individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged from the Dec 2031 rule: ≥80% PDC, a verified weight every 6 months, ≥5% loss at 6 months or a clinician override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, a 90-day bone pause, and a 6-month suspension after two misses. The Indiana and Arkansas 12-month rules continue. Private gating covers ~75% of employer plans. BMI-linked wellness surcharges up to 30% continue. AUD-route users are outside weigh-in verification. CMS has warned about diagnosis coding but has not issued a rule.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening keeps pushing drivers toward tirzepatide. Fleets screen drivers on gray vials as an insurance matter. Army accession is still contested and the Air Force waiver stands. The VA adopted semaglutide for AUD in its formulary within a month of approval.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API supplies most gray retatrutide and cagrilintide. Indian finished semaglutide floods mail channels while US ANDAs stall. Section 232 tariffs remain and are still cited. Retatrutide allocation eased with new North Carolina fill-finish capacity.

events.event: FDA issues complete response letters to the first four generic semaglutide applications, citing impurity and immunogenicity data for synthetic peptide; the 2033 entry date set by settlement passes with no US generic and portal prices stay at $199–279

A month after the American Society of Addiction Medicine endorses semaglutide for moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder on two phase 3 trials, Novo files for the indication and drug compendia list the use

CMS guidance confirms compendia-supported AUD use is covered under standard Part D and Medicaid substance-use benefits, outside the obesity continuation standard; nine more states have taken the 90% Medicaid match, bringing the total to 40 plus DC

A Philadelphia federal jury awards $41 million to a woman claiming persistent gastroparesis in the first bellwether of the GLP-1 GI litigation, which now exceeds 52,000 filed cases; a June bellwether goes for the defence

DOJ and FDA shut a Tampa-based 'peptide clinic' network that sold research-use retatrutide vials and video reconstitution coaching to about 180,000 customers; FDA estimates 2.4 million Americans now use unapproved research-grade incretins
FDA approves semaglutide 2.4 mg for alcohol use disorder regardless of weight; within weeks 'Unhooked' launches an on-label telehealth intake and two HR platforms list it beside 'focus' subscriptions
events.driver: new_indications: alcohol_use_disorder; personality_layer: marketed_feature; cultural_response: normalisation

open_tensions: The AUD route has become a side door. A patient cut off by the obesity continuation standard or a gated employer plan can be re-prescribed the same molecule after a ten-question drinking screen, without weigh-ins. CMS has warned about coding but has written no rule, and employers are adding exclusions one plan at a time.

Generic semaglutide is still absent after the 2033 date. Public programs pay $199 on ≈34M users, about $82B a year gross. Meanwhile ≈7M Americans use gray product, 2.4M of them on unapproved research-grade molecules with no DEXA, no SHAPS and no lot testing. Congress has not legalised import and has not sealed the mail.

The GI mass tort now has more than 52,000 cases and split bellwethers. Plaintiffs' advertising is teaching millions of users that their nausea may be worth money, while the epidemiology on persistence after stopping is unresolved. Neither settlement nor label science can move faster than the other.

Medicare's 65+ user base rose to 17.75M and excess hip fractures to ≈17,800 a year. The drug is billed to Part D at ≈$46B a year, while fracture and fall care lands on Part A and MA, and no CBO score covers both.
still_true: Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.

The Part D obesity benefit still pays a $199 negotiated rate with a $50 beneficiary copay, and the CMS 90-day 'bone pause' code still applies only to Medicare and enhanced-match Medicaid, not to private gated plans.
The 503B exclusion and the 503A injunction on compounded incretins stand, and individual users of imported or gray product are still not prosecuted.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: One in Three, Still No Generic: America's Drug Gets a Bar Tab, 52,000 Lawsuits and a Vial Market in Every Strip Mall
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 almost one American adult in three is on an incretin drug. Over forty, it is simply assumed. People who are off are expected to give a reason, and the acceptable reasons now include one that did not exist two years ago: 'my stomach'. The lawyers made that respectable. The federal GI litigation in Philadelphia has passed fifty-two thousand cases. In March a jury gave a woman with persistent gastroparesis forty-one million dollars, and in June a different jury gave another plaintiff nothing. Ads run during the evening news asking whether your nausea was ever explained to you. The science on whether the stomach recovers after stopping is still unresolved, and the court calendar will not wait for it.

The generic everyone budgeted for did not come. The 2033 entry date that Novo signed in 2031 arrived, and the FDA sent the first four generic applicants back for more data on synthetic peptide impurities. The pen is still $199. The oral starter is still $149. Nobody in Washington reopened price talks. Both parties ran 'where's the generic?' ads in the midterms anyway.

The growth in use came from who pays. Nine more states took the ninety-percent Medicaid match, bringing the total to forty plus Washington, D.C. Medicare now covers nearly eighteen million users over sixty-five. Public programs together pay for close to two fills in five, so for anyone old or poor the government is the default payer. The continuation standard has not changed. It still means kiosk weigh-ins, a five-percent threshold, annual scans for long-term seniors and a ninety-day bone pause. Private gated plans still have no pause.

Then alcohol became an indication. Addiction physicians endorsed semaglutide for alcohol use disorder in mid-2033, Medicare and Medicaid agreed to pay for that use outside the weigh-in rules, and in September the FDA approved it for drinkers of any weight. The label is the first to mention reward-related effects. Within weeks 'Unhooked', the telehealth brand that already sold 'craving freedom', was running an on-label intake built on a ten-question drinking screen. Doctors noticed quickly that a patient dropped for missing a weigh-in can return through the drinking door. CMS has warned about coding and has written no rule.

The heaviest drinkers were always most of the market, so spirits are falling faster than ever. In Wisconsin, taverns close at twice the old rate, and the brandy old fashioned at the Friday fish fry is often non-alcoholic now. On Nashville's Lower Broadway, bars that ran on drink sales have raised cover charges and cut sets. First dates happen over coffee.

The gray market is back, in a different form. No pharmacy can compound, so storefront 'peptide clinics' sell vials of Chinese-made retatrutide labelled for research use, with a video call to show you how to mix it. About seven million Americans use something unapproved or imported, and around two and a half million of them are on molecules no regulator has looked at for that use. In May federal agents closed a Tampa network with a hundred and eighty thousand customers. There were similar storefronts in Houston and Phoenix the following week.

The bone problem is growing as the users age. The latest estimate is nearly eighteen thousand excess hip fractures a year. Mobile DEXA vans have doubled, and waits are a little shorter. About five million people who are not overweight pay for calm or focus, and the first independent survey found a small difference in blunting that did not reach significance. Most people are fine. The ones who aren't are easy to miss.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tammy Wendt is fifty-six and runs the front desk of a dental office in Green Bay. At 6:10 she draws 0.4 from a vial labelled RESEARCH USE ONLY into an insulin syringe at the kitchen counter, the way the woman on the video showed her. It costs $120 a month from a clinic in Tampa that changed its name in June. Her employer plan dropped her in March. She had taken her bone pause like the endocrinologist said, missed the kiosk window, and that was that.

She checks her phone. The Tampa clinic has emailed: new lot shipping, same price, please update your saved card. She updates it.
